instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company has 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Employees sign in with user accounts in an Active Directory domain in the company's data center. The data center already connects to a VPC through AWS Direct Connect. The employees must use their existing Active Directory credentials to access the AWS accounts. The company does not want to run domain controllers in AWS or to keep copies of the users or passwords in AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create IAM users in each AWS account with a script that copies the user names from Active Directory, and require MFA for each IAM user.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure SAML 2.0 federation from an AD FS server in the data center to an IAM identity provider and IAM roles in each AWS account.

options.label: C
options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, and create a trust relationship with the on-premises domain.

options.label: D
options.text: Use IAM Identity Center with AD Connector as the identity source, and assign permission sets to Active Directory groups for the AWS accounts.
